item.title: Iran's nuclear timeline unchanged despite war, US intel finds
item.description: Two months into a U.S.-led military campaign against Iran, American intelligence assessments indicate that the time Tehran would need to build a nuclear weapon has not shifted since last summer, when a joint U.S.-Israeli strike extended the timeline to roughly nine months to a year, Reuters reported on Monday, citing three sources familiar with the matter.

item.title: Pentagon says Iran attacks on US forces 'below threshold' to restart war
item.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared Tuesday that the US-Iran ceasefire remains intact despite a sharp escalation of hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz, telling reporters at a Pentagon press briefing that "the ceasefire is not over" even as Iran has attacked American forces more than 10 times since the truce began on April 7.

Gen. Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said the attacks remain "below the threshold for recommencing significant combat operations," adding that Iran has also fired on commercial vessels nine times and seized two container ships during the ceasefire period. "The decision to restart operations is a political one beyond my authority," Caine said. "Currently, what we are experiencing is minor harassing fire. It seems as though Iran is clutching at straws".

item.title: US military confirms loss of KC-135 tanker over Persian Gulf
item.description: A US Air Force KC-135 Stratotanker vanished from radar over the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday after broadcasting a 7700 emergency distress signal, raising alarm on the second day of Operation Project Freedom, the American military operation to guide commercial ships through the contested waterway.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine declare competing ceasefires after drone hits Moscow tower
item.description: A Ukrainian drone slammed into a luxury high-rise residential tower in southwestern Moscow early Monday, breaching the Russian capital's air defenses in one of the most brazen strikes on the city since the full-scale war began. The attack came just five days before Russia's annual Victory Day parade on May 9 and hours before Moscow declared a unilateral ceasefire for the holiday.

item.title: Pentagon says Iran ceasefire 'still intact' despite clashes in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: President Donald Trump warned on Monday that Iran would be "blown off the face of the Earth" if its forces targeted American vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as the fragile ceasefire between the two nations appeared to buckle under escalating military clashes tied to the U.S.-led naval escort operation known as Project Freedom.

item.title: Rubio says Taiwan will come up at Trump-Xi summit next week
item.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed on Tuesday that Taiwan will be a topic of discussion when President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14-15, warning against any "destabilizing" actions regarding the self-governing island as the high-stakes summit approaches.

"I'm sure Taiwan will be a topic of conversation; it always is," Rubio said during a White House press briefing, adding that neither Washington nor Beijing has an interest in seeing instability in the Indo-Pacific region.

item.title: Rubio calls Israel-Lebanon peace 'imminently achievable'
item.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared Tuesday that a peace deal between Israel and Lebanon is "imminently achievable," while identifying Hezbollah as the central obstacle to any lasting agreement between the two nations.

"By and large, I think a peace deal between Lebanon and Israel is imminently achievable, and should be," Rubio told reporters at a White House press briefing. "The problem with Israel and Lebanon is not Israel or Lebanon, it's Hezbollah."

item.title: Cargo vessel hit in Strait of Hormuz amid US 'Project Freedom' launch
item.description: A cargo vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to a report from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency, Reuters reported. The attack marks the latest in a string of maritime incidents in one of the world's most critical shipping lanes, as the United States pursues a new military initiative to reopen the waterway.

item.title: US fires Tomahawk from Typhon launcher in Philippines for the first time
item.description:
The U.S. Army fired a Tomahawk cruise missile from its Typhon mid-range capability system on Philippine soil for the first time early Tuesday, launching from Tacloban City Airport on Leyte Island and striking a target roughly 600 kilometers (about 370 miles) away at Fort Magsaysay in Laur, Nueva Ecija, on the island of Luzon.

The test came as China responded with a show of force over the disputed South China Sea, deploying H-6 bombers and J-16 fighter jets over Scarborough Shoal in what Beijing called "combat readiness" patrols.

item.title: Trump pauses Hormuz escort operation, citing Iran deal progress
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that he is temporarily pausing "Project Freedom," the U.S. military operation to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz, just one day after it launched. Trump cited "great progress" toward a deal with Iran and requests from mediator Pakistan and other countries, even as the naval blockade on Iranian ports remains fully in force.

The pause came after a turbulent 24 hours in which the operation's launch on Monday triggered Iranian warning shots, attacks on commercial vessels, and strikes on Gulf states — escalating tensions that threatened to unravel the fragile ceasefire in place since April 7.

item.title: Spain to repatriate all passengers from hantavirus cruise ship
item.description: All passengers and crew remaining aboard the MV Hondius, a luxury expedition cruise ship struck by a deadly hantavirus outbreak, are currently asymptomatic, Spanish Health Minister Mónica García announced on Wednesday. The ship, which has been anchored near Cape Verde after being denied permission to dock, will now proceed to the Port of Granadilla in southern Tenerife, where passengers will be repatriated to their home countries.

item.title: Trump pauses Iran strikes, warns of escalation if no deal
item.description: Iran confirmed on Wednesday that it is formally evaluating a US peace proposal as the two sides inch toward what a Pakistani mediator has described as a potential agreement to end the nearly 10-week war. President Donald Trump announced a temporary pause of "Project Freedom," the US military operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, citing "great progress" toward a deal — but warned that bombing would resume "at a much higher level and intensity" if Tehran refuses to come to terms.

item.title: China's Big Fund in talks to lead DeepSeek round at $45B valuation
item.description:
China's largest state-backed semiconductor investment vehicle is in advanced negotiations to lead the first external funding round for AI startup DeepSeek at a valuation of approximately $45 billion, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing four people familiar with the discussions.

The China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund — known in the industry as the "Big Fund" — would mark a dramatic expansion of its mandate, which has historically focused on chip fabrication, memory producers, and semiconductor equipment rather than AI model labs.

item.title: French container ship hit by missile in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
French shipping giant CMA CGM confirmed on Wednesday that its Maltese-flagged container vessel, the CMA CGM San Antonio, was struck during an attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, injuring several crew members and damaging the ship.

U.S. officials told CBS News the vessel was hit by what they described as a possible land-attack cruise missile late Tuesday evening local time, with several Filipino crew members among the injured. The wounded were evacuated and are receiving medical treatment, the company said in a statement to AFP.

item.title: North Korea drops reunification from constitution, codifies Kim's nuclear authority
item.description:
North Korea has revised its constitution to remove all references to reunification with South Korea, formally codifying leader Kim Jong Un's doctrine of treating the two Koreas as hostile, separate states, according to a draft of the amended text reviewed by Reuters.

The revision, believed to have been adopted during a March session of the Supreme People's Assembly, marks the first time North Korea has included a territorial clause in its constitution, Seoul National University professor Lee Jung-chul said at a South Korean Unification Ministry briefing on Wednesday.

item.title: Ukraine says Russia violated ceasefire with overnight strikes
item.description: Ukraine accused Russia on Wednesday of breaching the unilateral ceasefire declared by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, with Russian forces launching 108 drones and three missiles at Ukrainian territory in the hours after the truce took effect at midnight on the night of May 5-6.

item.title: Ted Turner, CNN founder and media mogul, dies at 87
item.description: Ted Turner, the maverick media mogul who founded CNN and transformed the landscape of American television, died Wednesday at age 87, according to Turner Enterprises. Turner, who had been living with Lewy body dementia since 2018, died at his home near Tallahassee, Florida.

item.title: Ted Turner, CNN founder and media mogul, dies at 87
item.description: Ted Turner, the brash media entrepreneur who launched the world's first 24-hour cable news network and reshaped how Americans consumed television, died Wednesday at age 87, according to Turner Enterprises. Turner died at his home near Tallahassee, Florida.

item.title: Shipping industry balks at Hormuz transit despite IRGC safe-passage pledge
item.description: Shipping companies are holding firm against resuming normal transits through the Strait of Hormuz, even as Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced "new protocols" for safe passage and signs of a potential U.S.-Iran peace agreement emerge following President Trump's pause of military operations in the waterway.

item.title: US, Iran near 14-point memo to end Gulf war, awaiting Tehran's response
item.description: Iran confirmed on Wednesday that it is evaluating a new 14-point US proposal aimed at ending the more than two-month-long Gulf conflict, even as President Donald Trump warned that military action could resume at a higher intensity if Tehran rejects the terms.
